MRI RIGHT KNEE

Clinical details: 45-year-old. Valgus injury skiing three weeks ago. Medial knee pain and tenderness over the medial joint line.

Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the right knee at 3T.

Comparison: No previous imaging available for comparison.

Findings:
Menisci: Both menisci are intact. No displaced meniscal fragment.
Cruciate ligaments: The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.
Collateral ligaments: Thickening and intermediate signal of the proximal medial collateral ligament with periligamentous oedema, fibres in continuity, in keeping with a grade 2 sprain. The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact.
Extensor mechanism: The extensor mechanism is unremarkable. Patellofemoral alignment is normal.
Articular cartilage: Articular cartilage is preserved in all three compartments.
Bone marrow: Mild bone marrow oedema of the lateral femoral condyle, in keeping with a contusion. No fracture.
Joint and soft tissues: Small joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. Mild medial subcutaneous oedema.

Impression:
1. Grade 2 sprain of the proximal medial collateral ligament.
2. Lateral femoral condyle bone contusion. Menisci and cruciate ligaments intact.
